spec_match.rationale: The generated rule uses the real CSS Values 5 surfaces — random(0%,100%), the by <step> argument, and the --size dashed-ident cache key for square sizing — and applies it through an adopted stylesheet when the browser parses it.

interactive.rationale: Count, min/max size and snap sliders plus Regenerate/Reset all rebuild the field and the displayed rule; each dot is tagged data-placed-by so the active path is inspectable.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises regenerate-on-change plus a comparison with the JavaScript alternative, and both are on the page.

edge_cases.rationale: The unsupported fallback is honest and labelled, but degenerate inputs (min ≥ max is silently clamped without narration) and the empty/step-larger-than-range cases are not surfaced.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5324559251275776 and the CSS Values 5 random() section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers parse of every argument form plus behavioural per-element-distinctness and fixed-collapses assertions — real contracts, not existence checks.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: banner correctly says random() is unsupported and falling back to JavaScript; 60 dots with data-placed-by=javascript and 20/20 distinct sampled top values; count slider to 100 rebuilt 100 dots; step slider rewrote the rule to 'top: random(0%, 100%, by 10%)'; console clean, no exceptions; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Builds log and emit showcaseTelemetry.assert('scatter-built', …) with count, support flag and step.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, secondary button overrides background and color together, 44px controls, live stage rather than a static card.

accessibility.rationale: Sliders are labelled with visible values, the field is role=img described by a text summary that updates with the parameters, and the readout is an aria-live output.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP, with unclipped controls in both screenshots.

openQuestions.title: Verify on a random()-supporting build that Regenerate actually re-rolls
openQuestions.detail: The supported path assumes sheet.replaceSync() with identical rule text forces fresh random() values ('a fresh computation gives fresh numbers'). CSS Values 5's random-caching is specified so values are stable per (element, occurrence) for the document's lifetime, so replacing the stylesheet with the same text may legally return the same values — in which case Regenerate would silently do nothing on Chrome 155 while working in the JS fallback. Chromium 141 cannot exercise this branch (random() unsupported here, so the claim was not browser-verifiable in this review). Verify on Chrome 155/Canary; if values do not re-roll, rebuild the dots (new elements get new per-element values) or perturb the rule, and correct the comment.

openQuestions.title: Narrate the min/max clamp
openQuestions.detail: When the smallest-size slider is pushed at or above the largest, the code clamps max to min+2 silently while the labels still show the raw slider values, so the displayed rule and the labels can disagree by a pixel or two. Either move the max slider's value or state the clamp in the readout.

summary: Canonical-use demo verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/css-random-function/scatter-field/: honest unsupported banner, JS fallback placing dots with genuinely distinct positions, rule text tracking every control including the by-step argument, clean console, both device classes overflow-free. Feature /conformance/ route ran 0 pass / 8 fail — all honest pre-155 gaps. Main open question is the supported-path assumption that replacing the adopted stylesheet re-rolls random() values, which contradicts the spec's stability rule and could make Regenerate a no-op on real Chrome 155.
